places.name: Het Schip
places.note: Michel de Klerk's brick ship of social housing, the high point of the Amsterdam School. The museum includes a restored worker's flat.

places.name: Museum Van Loon
places.note: A canal house still owned by its family, with a formal garden and a coach house behind. The canal-ring life, from the inside.

places.name: Begijnhof
places.note: A hidden courtyard of almshouses off the Spui, home to one of the city's two surviving wooden houses. Enter quietly; people live here.

places.name: Athenaeum Boekhandel
places.note: A bookshop and newsroom on the Spui, with international magazines by the wall. Pair it with the Begijnhof next door.

places.name: Café 't Smalle
places.note: A brown café in an 18th-century jenever distillery, with a few tables on a canal-side jetty. Arrive early on a fine afternoon.

places.name: Rijksmuseum Library
places.note: Cuypers' cast-iron library of galleries and spiral stairs, inside the Rijksmuseum. Find it after the Night Watch.

places.name: Stedelijk Museum
places.note: Modern art and design, in a 19th-century building joined to a white 'bathtub' wing. Strong on Mondrian, Rietveld and De Stijl.

places.name: Eye Filmmuseum
places.note: A white angular hull on the far bank of the IJ. Take the free ferry from Centraal, watch a film, then a drink by the water.

places.name: Hortus Botanicus
places.note: One of the world's oldest botanical gardens, with a glasshouse of three climates. A green pause in the Plantage.

places.name: De Kas
places.note: Dinner in a 1920s municipal greenhouse, cooking from what grows in its own beds. Light, glass and vegetables.

places.name: Van Gogh Museum
places.note: Rietveld's building and Kurokawa's oval wing, holding the largest Van Gogh collection. Book the first slot.

places.name: Rembrandt House
places.note: The house where Rembrandt lived and worked, his studio and cabinet of curiosities restored. Etching demonstrations most days.

places.name: Our Lord in the Attic
places.note: A hidden Catholic church in the attic of a canal house, from when Catholic worship was banned. Astonishing.

places.name: Huis Marseille
places.note: Photography across two connected canal houses with a garden. Calm and well curated.

places.name: Foam
places.note: Photography in a canal house, with young photographers alongside the masters.

places.name: Het Scheepvaartmuseum
places.note: A naval storehouse with a glass courtyard roof patterned like a nautical chart. A replica East Indiaman moored outside.

places.name: NEMO
places.note: Renzo Piano's green copper ship's hull rising out of the harbour. The sloping roof is a public square.

places.name: Westerkerk
places.note: Rembrandt is buried here somewhere. Climb the tower for the city's best view.

places.name: Oude Kerk
places.note: The city's oldest building, a wooden-vaulted church now hosting contemporary art. Surrounded by the red-light district.

places.name: Stadsarchief (De Bazel)
places.note: A brick bank of 1926 in Amsterdam School style, now the city archive. The treasury vault is open to visitors.

places.name: Vondelpark
places.note: The city's park: lawns, ponds and an open-air theatre. Hire a bike and drift.

places.name: Westergasfabriek
places.note: A gasworks turned park, with cafés, cinemas and events in the old industrial buildings.

places.name: NDSM Wharf
places.note: A shipyard turned artists' city on the IJ. Take the free ferry, see the street art, eat on the water.

places.name: Noordermarkt
places.note: A Saturday farmers' market and a Monday flea market around a church. Apple pie at Winkel 43 nearby.

places.name: Concertgebouw
places.note: The great hall with celebrated acoustics. Look out for the free lunchtime concerts.

places.name: Pathé Tuschinski
places.note: A 1921 picture palace of Art Deco and Amsterdam School excess. See any film in the main hall.

places.name: Café Hoppe
places.note: A brown café since 1670, with sand on the floor. Drinkers spill onto the Spui.

places.name: In 't Aepjen
places.note: A bar in one of the city's two surviving wooden houses. Low beams, old genever.

places.name: Winkel 43
places.note: The city's favourite apple pie, tall and spiced, with whipped cream. Best on market days.

places.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
places.note: A brewery beside the De Gooyer windmill. Tasting room inside, terrace outside.
